@ a condition slower than W is read by holding it: the part runs from the frame where the held value holds, and the stage of sample / 2 inside it counts the runs
@ a held condition that changes: the stopped stretches keep the last output, and the delays of the part count its runs
- a slow condition that always holds is the same as no when~: a chain and a conversion flow
- a conversion flow whose condition is slower than its output: the grids that are stopped keep the output, and the window is the 4 samples the part ran
@ x.down~(4).when~(m8 != 2) and x.when~(m8 != 2).down~(4) give the same values: W is sample / 4 in both, and m8 is read held at the grid
@ x.when~(l).up~(2) with a slow condition: W is sample * 2, the condition is held and read in both runs of a frame
@ a when~ with a slow condition inside an arm of if~ goes on whether the arm is taken or not
process 0 frames=12 in c=[true false true false true false true false true false true false]
@ a when~ with a slow condition in the body of a par~: each replica holds the condition it reads and counts its own runs
@ sample_tick() in a condition is the time of the body's sample: the frame index, the same in both runs of an up, and at the grid of sample / 4 the time of the grid (S-1218)
@ the calls of process cut the frames in the middle of a grid, a run and a stopped stretch, and a reset starts over: the same values (§13.4, §11.6)
@ sample_tick() in a condition read at sample / 4 takes that clock with no at, as with an at to it (§11.4: the tick clock of the place it is used, up to sample / N)
